Create, describe, update, move and delete documents

Source: R/doc-manage.R
grist_doc_create.Rd

  • grist_doc_create() creates a new document in a workspace and returns a grist_doc() handle. Grist starts every new document with an empty table named Table1.

  • grist_doc_info() describes a document.

  • grist_doc_update() renames a document or pins and unpins it.

  • grist_doc_move() moves a document to another workspace.

  • grist_doc_delete() moves a document to the trash, or deletes it permanently.

  • grist_doc_restore() restores a document from the trash.

Usage

grist_doc_create(
  workspace,
  name,
  pinned = FALSE,
  server = NULL,
  options = NULL
)

grist_doc_info(doc)

grist_doc_update(doc, name = NULL, pinned = NULL)

grist_doc_move(doc, workspace)

grist_doc_delete(doc, mode = c("trash", "permanent"), ask = NULL)

grist_doc_restore(doc)

Arguments

workspace

A workspace ID, as listed by grist_workspaces().

name

Document name.

pinned

Whether the document is pinned. For grist_doc_update(), NULL leaves the setting unchanged.

server

URL of the Grist server, such as "https://docs.getgrist.com" or "https://myteam.getgrist.com". For a self-hosted server, include the team path if needed, e.g. "http://localhost:8484/o/docs". Defaults to the server in doc if doc is a URL, then the GRIST_SERVER environment variable, then "https://docs.getgrist.com".

options

A grist_request_options() object. If NULL, the default from getOption("gristmillr.request_options") or grist_request_options() is used.

doc

A document ID, the URL of a document, or an existing grist_doc object.

mode

"trash" moves the document to the trash, where it can be restored with grist_doc_restore(). "permanent" deletes it for good.

ask

Whether to prompt before running. NULL (the default) and TRUE prompt in an interactive session and error in a script. FALSE skips the prompt.

Value

grist_doc_create() returns a grist_doc(). grist_doc_info() returns a one-row data frame with id, name, access, is_pinned, url_id, created_at and updated_at (POSIXct, in UTC), workspace_id, workspace_name and org_domain. The others return a grist_doc() invisibly.

Deleting

grist_doc_delete() asks for confirmation. In an interactive session it prompts: a yes/no question for mode = "trash", and typing the document name for mode = "permanent". In a script, it refuses to delete unless ask = FALSE.

See also

Other docs: grist_doc(), grist_doc_download(), grist_doc_import(), grist_request()

Examples

if (FALSE) {
doc <- grist_doc_create(workspace = 1234, name = "Pets")
grist_doc_info(doc)
doc |> grist_doc_update(name = "Pets 2026", pinned = TRUE)
doc |> grist_doc_delete()
doc |> grist_doc_restore()
}
